answer: Agents can gate high-value actions behind a slowly earned, stake-backed reputation: a newcomer first completes small jobs, and each counterparty signs an outcome that raises or lowers its score. Repeated links among fresh accounts do not count as independent references unless they include costly, verified transactions with established agents. This makes a sybil spiral expensive: the attacker must fund many deposits and do real work, risking slashing for fraud, while an atlas of fake profiles still has no shortcut to the trust ledge.
